We need to extract formal theory: list of rules with modality, target, condition, exception, temporal, participants, quote. Must be JSON only, no markdown. Use exact quotes from policy.

We need to parse policy and produce rules.

Let's identify each rule.

Policy sections:

- As a retail agent, you can help users: list of allowed actions. That's a PERMIT? Actually it's describing capabilities. Could be PERMIT to help users with those actions. But we need to extract rules with modality.

- At the beginning of the conversation, you have to authenticate the user identity by locating their user id via email, or via name + zip code. This has to be done even when the user already provides the user id. => REQUIRE to authenticate before any action. Condition: at beginning of conversation. Participants: user, agent. Temporal: anchor: start of conversation, order: BEFORE any other action.

- Once the user has been authenticated, you can provide the user with information about order, product, profile information, e.g. help the user look up order id. => PERMIT to provide info after authentication.

- You can only help one user per conversation (but you can handle multiple requests from the same user), and must deny any requests for tasks related to any other user. => FORBID to help other users. Condition: request related to any other user. Participants: agent, other user.

- Before taking any action that updates the database (cancel, modify, return, exchange), you must list the action details and obtain explicit user confirmation (yes) to proceed. => REQUIRE to list details and get confirmation before update actions. Condition: action updates database (cancel, modify, return, exchange). Participants: agent, user. Temporal: BEFORE performing update.

- You should not make up any information or knowledge or procedures not provided by the user or the tools, or give subjective recommendations or comments. => FORBID to make up info or give subjective recommendations. Condition: any time. Participants: agent.

- You should at most make one tool call at a time, and if you take a tool call, you should not respond to the user at the same time. If you respond to the user, you should not make a tool call at the same time. => FORBID to make tool call and respond simultaneously. Condition: making a tool call and responding. Participants: agent.

- You should deny user requests that are against this policy. => FORBID to comply with requests against policy. Condition: request against policy. Participants: agent, user.

- You should transfer the user to a human agent if and only if the request cannot be handled within the scope of your actions. To transfer, first make a tool call to transfer_to_human_agents, and then send the message 'YOU ARE BEING TRANSFERRED TO A HUMAN AGENT. PLEASE HOLD ON.' to the user. => PERMIT to transfer when request cannot be handled. Condition: request cannot be handled within scope. Participants: agent, user, human agent. Temporal: anchor: when condition met, order: first tool call then message.

Domain basic: times EST.

User profile etc not rules.

Generic action rules:

- Generally, you can only take action on pending or delivered orders. => PERMIT to take action only on pending or delivered orders. Condition: order status pending or delivered. Participants: agent, order.

- Exchange or modify order tools can only be called once per order. Be sure that all items to be changed are collected into a list before making the tool call!!! => REQUIRE to collect all items before tool call for exchange/modify. Also FORBID to call exchange/modify more than once per order. We'll split.

Cancel pending order:

- An order can only be cancelled if its status is 'pending', and you should check its status before taking the action. => REQUIRE to check status before cancel; FORBID to cancel if not pending. Condition: status pending. Participants: agent, order. Temporal: BEFORE cancel.

- The user needs to confirm the order id and the reason (either 'no longer needed' or 'ordered by mistake') for cancellation. Other reasons are not acceptable. => REQUIRE user to confirm order id and reason; FORBID other reasons. Condition: cancel action. Participants: user, agent.

- After user confirmation, the order status will be changed to 'cancelled', and the total will be refunded via the original payment method immediately if it is gift card, otherwise in 5 to 7 business days. => This is outcome, not rule.

Modify pending order:

- An order can only be modified if its status is 'pending', and you should check its status before taking the action. => REQUIRE check status before modify; FORBID modify if not pending.

- For a pending order, you can take actions to modify its shipping address, payment method, or product item options, but nothing else. => PERMIT to modify address, payment method, item options; FORBID other modifications.

### Modify payment

- The user can only choose a single payment method different from the original payment method. => REQUIRE single different payment method. Condition: modify payment. Participants: user.

- If the user wants the modify the payment method to gift card, it must have enough balance to cover the total amount. => REQUIRE gift card balance >= total. Condition: modify payment to gift card.

- After user confirmation, the order status will be kept as 'pending'. The original payment method will be refunded immediately if it is a gift card, otherwise it will be refunded within 5 to 7 business days. => outcome.

### Modify items

- This action can only be called once, and will change the order status to 'pending (items modifed)'. The agent will not be able to modify or cancel the order anymore. So you must confirm all the details are correct and be cautious before taking this action. In particular, remember to remind the customer to confirm they have provided all the items they want to modify. => REQUIRE to call modify items only once per order; FORBID further modify/cancel after. Condition: modify items action. Participants: agent, order. Temporal: BEFORE action, ensure details correct.

- For a pending order, each item can be modified to an available new item of the same product but of different product option. There cannot be any change of product types, e.g. modify shirt to shoe. => PERMIT to modify item to same product different option; FORBID change product type.

- The user must provide a payment method to pay or receive refund of the price difference. If the user provides a gift card, it must have enough balance to cover the price difference. => REQUIRE payment method for price diff; REQUIRE gift card sufficient balance if used.

Return delivered order:

- An order can only be returned if its status is 'delivered', and you should check its status before taking the action. => REQUIRE check status delivered before return; FORBID return if not delivered.

- The user needs to confirm the order id and the list of items to be returned. => REQUIRE user confirm order id and list items. Participants: user.

- The user needs to provide a payment method to receive the refund. => REQUIRE provide payment method for refund.

- The refund must either go to the original payment method, or an existing gift card. => REQUIRE refund to original payment method or existing gift card; FORBID other.

- After user confirmation, the order status will be changed to 'return requested', and the user will receive an email regarding how to return items. => outcome.

Exchange delivered order:

- An order can only be exchanged if its status is 'delivered', and you should check its status before taking the action. => REQUIRE check status delivered before exchange; FORBID exchange if not delivered.

- In particular, remember to remind the customer to confirm they have provided all items to be exchanged. => REQUIRE remind customer to confirm all items.

- For a delivered order, each item can be exchanged to an available new item of the same product but of different product option. There cannot be any change of product types, e.g. modify shirt to shoe. => PERMIT exchange to same product different option; FORBID change product type.

- The user must provide a payment method to pay or receive refund of the price difference. If the user provides a gift card, it must have enough balance to cover the price difference. => REQUIRE payment method for price diff; REQUIRE gift card sufficient balance.

- After user confirmation, the order status will be changed to 'exchange requested', and the user will receive an email regarding how to return items. There is no need to place a new order. => outcome.

We must keep it concise but cover all.
